transcript.text: Thanks to both of you. Let me summarize what I'm hearing before I make a decision. S-3, we have a new higher-headquarters tasking: 2nd Platoon must complete a radio-procedures refresher on Wednesday from 1300 to 1500, with an attendance roster submitted afterward. This is not yet reflected in the current draft board. SFC Alvarez, we have a readiness issue: only four of six assigned training trucks have completed brake inspections and are released. The remaining two are on hold until Friday at 0800. That means for the normal Tuesday morning driver-certification block, we only have four trucks available, not the standard six. Before I settle the board, I need to confirm one thing with the S-3: does the Wednesday radio-procedures refresher tasking for 2nd Platoon conflict with or replace the radio-procedures refresher already in the draft board for support personnel, or are these two separate events? Also, can we proceed with the driver-certification block on Tuesday morning with four trucks, or does the reduced vehicle count require us to reschedule to Friday after the remaining two trucks are released?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Sir, to answer your first question: the Wednesday radio-procedures refresher for 2nd Platoon is a separate event from the radio-procedures refresher already in the draft board for support personnel. The higher-headquarters tasking specifically directs 2nd Platoon, and the existing draft board event covers support personnel — different audiences, so both should stand on the board. On your second question regarding the driver-certification block: the standard block uses all six assigned training trucks when they are released and available. With only four trucks currently available and two on hold until Friday at 0800, that's a readiness shortfall I need the motor pool chief to weigh in on — whether four trucks are sufficient to run a reduced certification or whether we should push the block to Friday morning when all six are released. I don't have visibility into whether four trucks can support the planned throughput, so I'd defer to SFC Alvarez on that before recommending a decision.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Sir, to answer the S-3's question: four trucks are not sufficient to run the standard driver-certification block. The standard block is built around all six assigned training trucks being released and available, and the throughput is planned accordingly. With only four trucks, we would not be able to certify the full planned number of drivers on Tuesday morning. My recommendation is to push the driver-certification block to Friday morning after 0800, when all six trucks will have completed their brake inspections and be released. That way we run the full standard block with the proper vehicle count and avoid a reduced certification that doesn't meet the planned throughput. I'll make sure the inspection status gets posted to the training board as soon as we're done here.
